name: Prone Neck Extension
description: The prone neck extension is performed lying face-down on a bench with the head extending off the edge, using a plate on the back of the head to resist cervical extension. It targets the posterior neck musculature — the cervical erectors and upper trapezius fibers — building strength in the often-neglected extension pattern. Combined with the neck curl, it provides balanced cervical musculature development essential for spine stability and contact-sport performance.

execution.starting_position: Lie face-down (prone) on a flat bench with the head extending off one end. Hold a weight plate against the back of the head with both hands. Begin with the head flexed forward.
execution.setup_instructions: Begin with no weight (bodyweight only). Progress load conservatively over multiple weeks of training before adding any resistance.
steps: Step 1: Lie prone with the head extending off the bench, plate held to the back of the head.
Step 2: Begin from the flexed position (head angled toward the floor).
Step 3: Extend the head upward and backward into full cervical extension.
Step 4: Hold briefly at the top.
Step 5: Lower slowly back to the starting flexed position.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale on the extension, inhale on the descent.
common_mistakes: Using excessive range of motion — extend to a comfortable position, not maximum
Performing with any cervical pathology or acute pain
safety_considerations: Contraindicated with any disc issues, cervical stenosis, or acute neck pain
Always use controlled motion — never jerk or bounce
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: From cervical flexion (head down) to comfortable cervical extension (head up and back).
coaching_cues: Don't force the range — work to comfortable extension
Match this volume with neck curl work for balance
